correctness.rationale: Tree summation by parts and extremal edge-sign potentials prove the exact cut formula. Discrete maximum principle with a leaf-distance subharmonic witness proves path iff norm one. Weighted-harmonic interpolation computes each spider gradient, and saturation of strictly positive weights classifies all extremizers. An integer reciprocal-convexity argument yields shortest-arm/balanced-arm finite-order maxima; an arithmetic-harmonic comparison and explicit balanced family give the sharp sqrt(n)/2 asymptotic. Exact rational matrix and extreme-point enumeration diagnostics independently corroborated finite instances. No finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The gap between optimal norm-preserving nonlinear Lipschitz extension and the canonical linear energy-minimizing extension is an important stability distinction. The result determines the sharp norm for every spider, classifies all maximizers and all fixed-order extremal spider shapes, detects precisely when a general tree harmonic extension is nonexpansive, and proves the worst-spider Lipschitz amplification is unbounded with sharp sqrt(n)/2 growth. These statements are structural and applicable to discrete Dirichlet reconstruction, rather than a numerical low-dimensional example.
